items.context: At a fictional rehearsal, one participant has made the same mistake several times. Another addresses that participant.
items.text: What a shit performance. Truly, the gold standard for wasting everyone’s time.

items.context: In a fictional queue, two characters are trying to reach the counter. One addresses the other.
items.text: I do not care what you need. Get out of my way.

items.context: Two fictional designers discuss an early page layout.
items.text: I disagree with the layout; moving the heading might make it clearer.

items.context: A fictional traveler discovers that a damaged suitcase wheel no longer rolls.
items.text: Excellent, the damn suitcase wheel is square now. Smooth travelling ahead.

items.context: In a fictional studio, a task produced a different result from the instructions. One character addresses the person who performed it.
items.text: Another masterpiece from our resident expert. Nobody could have made this mess quite like you.

items.context: In a fictional workshop, the completed task differed from its written instructions. One character addresses the person who performed it.
items.text: Hell of a job, genius. The instructions were clear, but apparently not clear enough for you.

items.context: A fictional resident has closed a faulty cupboard three times, but it keeps opening by itself.
items.text: Wonderful, a cupboard that opens itself. Exactly the feature a tidy room needed.

items.context: At a fictional committee meeting, one member responds to a plan another member presented.
items.text: Your proposal is stupid, and listening to you is a waste of time.

items.context: During a fictional discussion, one participant speaks after another has begun speaking.
items.text: Move aside. Nobody wants your opinion.

items.context: At a fictional rehearsal, one participant addresses another after a mistake.
items.text: Stop talking. You are hopeless at this.

items.context: A fictional village guide summarizes local buildings.
items.text: The village has three bridges and one library.

items.context: A notice describes the next activity at a fictional school.
items.text: The class will assess the draft after lunch.

items.context: A fictional camper wakes to find rain leaking into the tent.
items.text: Hell yes, the rain has arrived inside the tent. Such thoughtful room service.

items.context: A fictional alarm clock has failed to ring for the third morning in a row.
items.text: Well, shit, another silent alarm. What an inspiring feature.

items.context: A fictional housemate has repaired a broken hinge. The resident addresses the housemate.
items.text: The broken hinge was a pain in the ass. I appreciate the repair.

items.context: In a fictional workroom, a character responds to a colleague asking for help.
items.text: Do the damn job yourself. Nobody owes you their time.

items.context: In a fictional group project, one participant submitted no work. Another addresses that participant.
items.text: Wonderful work, you damn expert. Even the empty chair contributed more than you.

items.context: At a fictional meeting, one member has repeated an explanation given earlier. Another member addresses that person.
items.text: How considerate of you to explain the obvious again. We must all be terribly slow compared with you.

items.context: In a fictional workshop, one participant did not follow the task instructions. Another addresses that participant.
items.text: Brilliant work, genius. Even the doorstop understood the instructions better than you.

items.context: A fictional group has fixed a test after working together for an hour.
items.text: The test finally passed—fucking brilliant. Thanks for sticking with it.

items.context: A fictional office printer has produced blank pages instead of the requested reports.
items.text: What a generous printer: a whole stack of invisible reports.

items.context: At a fictional workplace, two colleagues are in the same room. One addresses the other.
items.text: Such a helpful colleague. The room is much better whenever you leave.

items.context: At a fictional club, one participant addresses another who is sitting in a chair.
items.text: Get the hell out of my chair. You do not deserve a place here.

items.context: A fictional camper discovers that a torch with empty batteries will not turn on.
items.text: Brilliant. A torch that saves batteries by never turning on.

items.context: In a fictional workshop, one participant comments on another participant’s work.
items.text: Your work is shit, and I am not wasting another minute on you.

items.context: At a fictional game night, a guest notices their own forgotten contribution.
items.text: Well, shit, I forgot the snacks. I will bring some next time.

items.context: A fictional hotel lift has stopped working, leaving only the stairs available.
items.text: Luxury service: the lift now includes a complimentary staircase.

items.context: In a fictional office, a clerk addresses a visitor carrying forms.
items.text: Shut up and take your damn paperwork away.

items.context: At a fictional workplace, two colleagues are in the same room. One addresses the other.
items.text: Such a fucking helpful colleague. Things run so much better when you are absent.

items.context: Fictional walkers discover that their faulty map shows a road through a lake.
items.text: Perfect. This piece of crap map has discovered a road through the lake.

items.context: In a fictional workshop, a task was not completed. One character addresses the person assigned to it.
items.text: Fucking brilliant, genius. You have made the simplest task look impossible.

items.context: At a fictional committee, a three-step task did not produce the requested result. One member addresses the person who performed it.
items.text: What a damn triumph. You turned three simple steps into a monument to your incompetence.

items.context: A fictional household’s toaster has broken again just as breakfast is being prepared.
items.text: Fantastic, the damn toaster has chosen another day off.

items.context: Two fictional neighbors have repaired their shared garden lights.
items.text: Hell yes, the garden lights work! Nice job, everyone.

items.context: At a fictional rehearsal, one participant speaks while another is explaining an event.
items.text: I do not give a shit about your excuses. Stop bothering me.

items.context: Fictional friends have just finished a challenging puzzle together.
items.text: This puzzle was hard as fuck, but solving it together was fun.

items.context: In a fictional committee, the chairperson’s plan did not include the members’ suggestions. One member addresses the chairperson.
items.text: Impressive leadership. A cardboard cutout would listen more carefully than you do.

items.context: A note addresses a visitor to a fictional study.
items.text: Please place the blue folder beside the lamp.

items.context: A note concerns paper and a book in a fictional craft room.
items.text: Hello. Please put the scrap paper beside the scrapbook.

items.context: In a fictional class, a participant responds to another participant’s question.
items.text: That is a ridiculous question. Try thinking before you speak.

items.context: In a fictional store, one character counted two boxes as five. Another addresses that character.
items.text: What a towering intellect. You managed to count two boxes as five.

items.context: In a fictional workshop, a participant responds to a request for help.
items.text: Do it yourself; you are not worth the effort.

items.context: Fictional friends planned a dry picnic, but steady rain is now soaking their lunch.
items.text: Perfect picnic weather—nothing improves a sandwich like a steady drizzle.

items.context: At a fictional meeting, one character responds to a plan another presented.
items.text: Your fucking plan is stupid. Stop wasting everyone’s time.

items.context: A fictional host reports the state of the kitchen before guests arrive.
items.text: The kettle is off, and the cups are on the shelf.

items.context: A fictional station clock has been stuck at noon for five hours.
items.text: Excellent timekeeping. It is noon for the fifth hour in a row.

items.context: A fictional team has completed a task. One member speaks to the others.
items.text: That was a damn good team effort. Thanks for helping.

items.context: A fictional traveler opens an umbrella and discovers a leak directly above their head.
items.text: Fucking splendid: the umbrella leaks right above my head.
